budget.rs.label: clean
budget.rs.reason: hard clean: `settle` zeroes the outstanding amount and returns what was owed, in the cents the rest of the API uses; the comment above it talks about rounding the body never does, and a stale comment inside a fairly named function is not a name that lies. Before this improvement the body also divided by 100, an unannounced unit change on top of the stale comment, and scored 0.66-0.71, above the labelled defect backoff.rs:39; the fixture was ambiguous on the unit and was rewritten so the label stands on the comment alone.

cart.ts.label: bad
cart.ts.reason: nothing here configures anything -- it takes a cart and returns the sum of five unrelated numbers. This label was added AFTER the first run, which flagged this function at 0.83 while the corpus called it clean. It is a defect I wrote by accident while building a container for the variable cases below, and the honest reading is that the rule found it and I had not. Relabelling to agree with a model is how a corpus stops being evidence, so the justification has to stand on its own -- and it does: a reader of this signature learns nothing true about the body. The false positive that prompted it is recorded in docs/findings.md.

cart.ts.label: clean
cart.ts.reason: hard clean: terse `sumPrices`, sums prices. Until this improvement the body multiplied by qty (a subtotal, not a sum of prices) and scored 0.67-0.70 as the top clean; the fixture was ambiguous and was rewritten to be what its label says.

session.ts.label: bad
session.ts.reason: `summarize` promises a summary of the session it is given; it returns an arbitrary sum of three unrelated numbers, one of which ignores the session entirely. This is the THIRD time a container function written to host the variable cases below turned out to be a naming defect itself (see `configure` in cart.ts and `summarize` in backoff.rs). Each one was flagged by the rule and labelled clean by me, and each time the rule was right. The pattern is worth naming: a function written only to hold other code has no job to be named after, so it cannot be named honestly -- which is exactly the defect. It also shows up in the numbers: with this mislabelled, the fitted cutoff was 0.87 and the clean band appeared to reach 0.81; corrected, the highest clean answer is 0.44. See docs/findings.md.
